comment: Owner-allowance conformance fixture (extensions/EXT-8-allowance.md; SPEC.md 7.7, 19.3). Pins the places where two independent node implementations drift: the allowance document's shape and canonical serialization under the owner signature (tag agentmesh-allowance-v1), floor-rounded metering arithmetic, smallest-remaining ceiling precedence, the refusal field names, and both exhaustion behaviours. All signed vectors were generated with the TypeScript SDK's canonicalization and tagged signing. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: when a test against it fails, fix the implementation, and when the fixture itself is believed wrong, change it only with a spec change alongside.

identities.comment: The same published test vectors budget.json and signature-tags.json use, deliberately: they are not real identities and control nothing, and reusing them keeps any new private-key-shaped string out of the repository. Here the sender key plays the OWNER (owner_key, the signer) and the recipient key plays the AGENT the allowance governs.

document.comment: EXT-8 1: v is the integer 1; ceilings[].scope is a closed enum (task | context | day); amount_micro and per_1k_tokens_micro are non-negative integer micro-units (1,000,000 micro-units = one currency unit; no floats near money, ever); currency an ISO 4217 code; cost_model REQUIRED; on_exhausted one of refuse | ask_owner; optional task_id / context_id narrow a ceiling; absent fields are OMITTED in canonical JSON, never null. sig is base64url over signed_bytes_prefix + canonical (the prefix never appears in the document). Every invalid case except missing_sig carries a GENUINE owner signature over its own canonical bytes, so each one is invalid for exactly the single stated reason - shape rejection never depends on a signature failure.

valid.note: the reference vector: a per-task ceiling, a context ceiling narrowed to one event, and a day ceiling
a single day ceiling with the ask-owner exhaustion behaviour, in a second currency
task_id narrows the ceiling to one Task, and a zero amount is legal - a ceiling pinned shut

invalid.why: a node MUST NOT enforce an unsigned document, and MUST NOT treat a non-verifying one as absent - it fails closed (every ceiling exhausted) until a valid document replaces it
amount_micro must be an integer (19.3: no floats near money); the signature is genuine, so the float is the only fault
scope is a closed enum: task | context | day. A consumer MUST reject an unknown scope rather than ignore the ceiling - an ignored ceiling is an unenforced one
amount_micro must be non-negative (a pinned-shut ceiling is 0, never -1)
cost_model is REQUIRED - a ceiling without a declared conversion cannot be metered against, and a document that cannot be metered against enforces nothing

metering.comment: EXT-8 2: cost_micro = floor(tokens * per_1k_tokens_micro / 1000), integer arithmetic throughout. FLOOR, pinned: rounding toward zero means the node never charges a partial micro-unit against the owner's ceiling, and any two nodes that meter the same invocation agree to the micro-unit. Metered spend is accounted to the Task, its context_id, and the UTC calendar day of the metering instant.

cases.why: exact: one thousand tokens at the per-1k rate
0.999 floors to 0 - a single tiny invocation can meter as zero; the ceiling check uses the metered value, not a re-derivation
exact: no rounding when the product divides evenly

precedence.comment: EXT-8 2: every applicable ceiling applies at once. Specificity (task, then context, then day) decides what a ceiling COVERS - which spend is accounted against it - never which ceiling wins. The BINDING ceiling for an admission decision is whichever applicable ceiling has the smallest REMAINING amount (amount_micro minus the spend already accounted to that ceiling's scope). remaining_micro and binding_scope are pinned so implementations agree on the arithmetic, not just the verdict.

cases.why: the day ceiling has 100000 remaining against a 200000 estimate; the task ceiling's larger headroom is irrelevant - specificity never outranks the smaller remainder
the estimate exceeds the whole per-task ceiling even though the day has 9000000 left
a context ceiling narrowed by context_id constrains ONLY that context; work in a different context is measured against the remaining applicable ceilings alone
the same ceilings, but the work is inside the narrowed context: 50000 remaining binds
the task ceiling is the binding one (smallest remaining) and the estimate fits inside it, so the work is admitted

Equality admits: 'would exceed' is strict, and spending exactly the remaining balance is within the allowance. Pinned 2026-07-28 after two implementations faced this then-unpinned boundary independently.

refusal.comment: EXT-8 2 / SPEC.md 12.2, 19.3. The allowance-broke refusal is byte-identical to budget.json's budget_insufficient shape, deliberately: on the wire, a refusal driven by the responder's own spending policy is indistinguishable from one driven by a too-low offer. It is legal even against a request that offered no ceiling at all - the estimate is then a price quote, and a resubmission at or above it is acceptance (19.3).

budget_insufficient.note: details.estimate is a cost_ceiling-shaped object: the node's price for the work

exhaustion.comment: EXT-8 2: what a node does when admitting the work would cross a ceiling, keyed by the document's on_exhausted.

refuse.expect: refuse at admission with BUDGET_INSUFFICIENT carrying details.estimate (the refusal shape above); no owner interaction, no work performed

ask_owner.expect: do NOT refuse: hold the work unstarted and surface the question through the node's owner channel (the EXT-6 review surface); proceed only if the owner raises the ceiling, and refuse with the same BUDGET_INSUFFICIENT shape if the owner declines

not_covered.comment: Boundaries, written down so nobody mistakes them for gaps.
items: Whether a node's spend report is TRUE is unverifiable by design (7.7: honor-system spend). This fixture pins shapes and arithmetic, not honesty.
The platform-side rollups and the mesh.event.agent.allowance_exceeded flag (EXT-8 3) are facilitation over 19.2 receipts, not node behaviour; they are not pinned here.
Settlement, payment and charging are out of scope for the extension and for this fixture.
Cross-agent allowances do not exist: constraining someone else's agent is a contract (a budget on a signed request), not a config.
